chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Writing for Jimmie Lunceford: 'Jeep Rhythm'
summary: For Lunceford's band with Willie Smith, Joe Thomas, Snooky Young, Trummy Young and Gerald Wilson, Horace wrote the original 'Jeep Rhythm' during the war.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Thank you. Okay. I'm just going to run down the line here, if I may. Let's talk about them. What about Jimmy Lunceford. When -- approximately when was this and what sort of writing were you doing, what --
This was during the era when he had the great lead man, Willie Smith that later on was with Harry James, you know.

And he had -- oh, a great tenor player by the name of Joe Thomas, which I was quite instrumental in bringing him out of Columbus, Ohio. He was originally an alto saxophonist, and I switched him over to tenor because he had such a great drive.
Did he play on your band?
He was in my band, first.
I see. Maybe we mentioned that before.

Yes. And I made some things for Jimmy. I made some originals, and this is what he was more or less interested in, you know, and I made a thing called 'Jeep Rhythm,' and he recorded it, and it worked out quite well (unintelligible) to us because it was during the war that this thing came out. That's how I -- we arrived at that title, and it did fine.
That was an original of yours?
The band played it, man, so well, you know. They could play -- Snookie Young and, of course, Trummy Young, the great trombonist. And Gerald Wilson was in that band.
The great arranger. He did arranging, yes.
